item.title: Josh Jacobs could be on thin ice in Green Bay
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Throughout his off-field incident that resulted in a no-contest plea to misdemeanor battery, the Packers have remained steadfast in their support of running back Josh Jacobs.
item.content:encoded:
Throughout his off-field incident that resulted in a no-contest plea to misdemeanor battery, the Packers have remained steadfast in their support of running back Josh Jacobs.

That could now be changing.

The persistent presence of the Packers as one of the teams that have expressed some degree of interest in trading for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor suggests that they've at least pondered the possibility of swapping out Jacobs for Taylor.

Recent developments don't help Jacobs's cause.

Beyond the handcuff celebration that Jacobs tried to say wasn’t a handcuff celebration (but that video of the full celebration suggests was a handcuff celebration), Friday's release of police records indicating that at least three other women have accused Jacobs of domestic violence could shake the team's apparent resolve to keep him.

Throw in the fact that Jacobs is averaging 2.3 yards per carry in his two games back from a six-game stint on paid leave — including 1.9 yards per carry against the worst run defense in the league entering Thursday night's game — and it's possible that the Packers will realize that Jacobs is no longer good enough to justify a stubborn circling of the wagons.

Cutting Jacobs would raise the issue of termination pay as to the balance of his $10.2 million salary, and it would short-circuit the team's ability to seek partial repayment of signing-bonus money if/when (when) he's eventually suspended under the Personal Conduct Policy. For now, we won't delve into the full extent of the niceties of Article 30 of the CBA; at a minimum, the Packers would have some potential arguments aimed at cutting off his right to any termination pay.

Even if the Packers ultimately are on the hook for termination pay, it's a sunk cost. The question is whether they want to keep him on the team, in light of recent developments.

Again, they've been linked in multiple reports from ESPNFL to a trade for Jonathan Taylor. That alone is substantial evidence that they're considering a future without Jacobs that could begin sooner rather than later.

item.title: Reports: Packers targeting Week 12 for Micah Parsons return
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said this week that he hopes defensive end Micah Parsons starts practicing with the team next week and the team reportedly has a goal in mind for Parsons's return to game action.
item.content:encoded:
Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said this week that he hopes defensive end Micah Parsons starts practicing with the team next week and the team reportedly has a goal in mind for Parsons's return to game action.

According to multiple reports, the team is targeting Week 12 for Parsons to play his first game since tearing his ACL last season. The Packers will be in Los Angeles to face the Rams in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game on Wednesday, November 25.

If Parsons does return to practice next week, it would open a 21-day window for him to work with the team ahead of being activated. The Packers, who beat the Panthers on Thursday night this week, face the Patriots and Vikings before a bye week in Week 11.

That timeline would have Parsons back for the final seven games of the regular season and his presence should boost the chances of the Packers following up those games with playoff action.

item.title: Report: John Harbaugh called Amy Adams Strunk directly in an effort to land Jeffery Simmons
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Harbaugh's unconventional move failed to prevent Bears from doing deal with Titans.
item.content:encoded:
The trade that sent defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Titans to the Bears has an interesting — and unusual — postscript.

Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reports that Giants coach John Harbaugh directly called Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk in an effort to get Simmons to New York.

The call reportedly came after Giants G.M. Joe Schoen had contacted Titans G.M. Mike Borgonzi about Simmons, only to be told that the Titans weren't trading him.

As Jones notes, another G.M. who learned about the effort said it "violates a code" among football's decision-makers. One source in a key football position with one of the NFL's teams dubbed the effort "shameful."

Despite Borgonzi's claim from Thursday that the Titans weren't looking to trade Simmons until the Bears called on Wednesday night, Jones reports that the Titans' "braintrust" had a meeting on Tuesday during which they decided to start listening to offers for Simmons.

It's unclear whether Harbaugh made the call to Adams before or after Bears G.M. Ryan Poles offered a package that included a pair of first-round picks. We're told the Giants were willing to offer more than what the Bears ultimately sent to the Titans. (Of course, that's easy to say at this point.)

The entire situation underscores the value of pre-existing relationships when it comes to getting deals done. It was a point we discussed on Friday's PFT Live. In 2021, the trade that sent quarterback Matthew Stafford from the Lions to the Rams had a distinct "inside job" feel to it, given that Lions G.M. Brad Holmes had recently been hired from the Rams.

Other teams that would have been interested in attempting to acquire Stafford were surprised to learn that he had been quietly and quickly dealt to the Rams, who were able to tuck quarterback Jared Goff into the deal — and to discreetly attach extra compensation to get the Lions to take on a contract that, after only two seasons, the Rams had come to regret. The outcome prompted former Commanders G.M. Martin Mayhew to call every team in the league the following offseason to inquire as to whether their starting quarterback may be available in trade.

The ultimate question, when trades like this happen, is whether the relationship angle results in the team that gives up a key player getting as much as it could. If the Giants would have indeed offered more, shouldn't the Titans have fully explored that avenue? Ultimately, the longstanding relationship between Poles and Borgonzi may have superseded the effort to get as much as possible for Simmons.

item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Jeffery Simmons, DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson and more big-name NFL players are on the move.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, and PFT has you covered with news and analysis of every trade, potential trade, rumor of a trade and trade that won’t be happening.

Here’s what’s happening on the NFL trade front:

Jeffery Simmons to Bears: Chicago receives Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Tennessee will receive 2027 and 2028 first-round picks along with a fourth-round pick in 2027.

Quenton Nelson to Seahawks: The Seahawks will send a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick back to Indianapolis.

DeForest Buckner to 49ers: Indianapolis will receive a 2027 fourth-round pick from San Francisco.

Jonathan Taylor trade talks have picked up: The Colts may not be done making deals.

The Jets have reportedly rebuffed Garrett Wilson trade interest: The Jets are not expected to deal their top wideout.

The Colts are open for business: Indianapolis is building for the future after firing General Manager Chris Ballard. Jonathan Taylor hasn’t requested a trade. Josh Downs says he's "open to whatever."

Budda Baker's name surfaces in trade rumors: Baker says he hasn’t asked to be traded from Arizona and also hasn't asked not to be traded.

Brian Thomas is a name to watch: The Jaguars trading Thomas frequently comes up in trade rumors.

Garrett Wilson wants to remain a Jet: The talented receiver says he is hoping not to get traded.

item.title: Reports: Jets aren't open to trading Garrett Wilson
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jets made a pair of big trades ahead of the 2025 trade deadline and they've got a player whose name has come up as a possible target for other teams this year.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets made a pair of big trades ahead of the 2025 trade deadline and they've got a player whose name has come up as a possible target for other teams this year.

Wide receiver Garrett Wilson would make several offenses better equipped to make a run at postseason success and his frustration with the way this Jets season is playing out boiled over on the sideline during last Sunday's loss to the Dolphins. Wilson followed that up by saying he loves playing for the Jets, but would also like to experience life on a winning team.

At the moment, it looks like he'll have to hope that happens while he's in a Jets uniform. Multiple reports say the Jets have told other teams that Wilson is not available ahead of the November 10 deadline. The Jets already have three first-round picks in 2027 and believe that Wilson's presence along with additions they can make with those assets will better position the team to win games than dealing him away.

Word was similar out of Tennessee before the Bears offered a pair of first-rounders for Jeffery Simmons, so it's possible someone could change the Jets' minds but, for now, Wilson appears set to stay put.

item.title: Jonathan Taylor trade talks are "active and ongoing"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Seahawks, Packers, Broncos, Vikings, Giants are pegged as potential destinations.
item.content:encoded:
There are two ways to handle the trade of a cornerstone player. One, talk quietly to a minimal number of teams. Like the Titans did with defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Two, throw the doors open and try to get the best possible package of draft picks and/or players in return. Like the Colts are now doing with running back Jonathan Taylor.

Indianapolis has officially declared that Taylor is available, via a selective and strategic leak to ESPNFL. Trade talks are "active and ongoing," per the report.

The teams that have "expressed at least some level of interest" are the Broncos, Packers, Vikings, Giants, and Seahawks.

Last weekend's Sunday Splash! report that operated as the "everything must go" sign for the Colts pegged the Broncos, Packers, Vikings, and Seahawks as potentially interested teams in Taylor. The Giants (who are believed, we're told by multiple sources, to have been pursuing Simmons) are a new arrival. Which would possibly be bad news for second-year running back Cam Skattebo, who emerged from the doghouse last week with 124 rushing yards. (It wouldn't be a surprise if the Giants offered Skattebo to the Colts as part of the trade package, frankly.)

To the extent that tying four teams to the trade talks doesn't get the Colts maximum compensation, the new report notes that the Colts "would prefer" that Taylor stick around for their "rebuild."

If they really wanted Taylor, they wouldn't be fielding trade offers fo him.

The Colts reportedly are looking for a package similar to what the 49ers sent to the Panthers in 2022 for running back Christian McCaffrey: a second-round pick, a third-round pick, and a fourth-round pick in the 2023 draft and a fifth-round pick in the 2024 draft.

The next question is whether Taylor will play on Sunday. It's possible, in our view, the Colts will hold Taylor out of action on Sunday at Jacksonville, like the Cardinals did three weeks ago when they had a deal in place to trade receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Texans. Even without a deal, keeping Taylor out of the game would ensure that he won't get injured.

If that happens, rookie Seth McGowan would be the likely starter in Week 8. Last Sunday, the seventh-rounder who played for Kentucky last year had 11 carries for 48 yards in a 16-10 loss to the Vikings.

And the Vikings continue to make the most sense for Taylor. Especially since they had the best possible opportunity to scout him six days ago, when he had 18 carries for 95 yards and an Adrian Peterson-style 38-yard touchdown run.

If the Vikings add Taylor in the coming days, he'd likely make his debut as soon as next Monday night, when the Vikings host the Bills. And when they put Peterson in the team's Ring of Honor.

item.title: Philip Rivers on NC State job: "Nothing's imminent"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers has reportedly "emerged as the focus" of the NC State coaching search.
item.content:encoded:
Former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers has reportedly "emerged as the focus" of the NC State coaching search. On Friday night, he didn't do much to throw water on the possibility.

"I mean, shoot, NC State’s special to me," Rivers said after coaching his latest high-school game (via Ben Thomas of AL.com), "and, you know, Coach [Dave] Doren, shoot, what he did over 14 years, and all-time winningest coach is a — ton of respect and appreciation, you know, for how he went about it with the university, and, you know, there's nothing there at this point.  No, you understand — like I told you earlier in the week — you understand the chatter is out there. Gotta take it one day at a time, you know, is all I know. I'm excited this postseason with these guys here, and I guess it's like I told you last year, you know, you never say never, but there's nothing imminent."

Rivers said "nothing" three times before choosing "imminent" as the next word. He could have just stopped with "nothing," if there was nothing.

Clearly there's something. Even more clearly, Rivers wants to delay things until the playoff run is over at St. Michael's, the high school where he has coached since 2021.

Indeed, Rivers specifically mentioned that he's "really looking forward to trying to send this last group off" with a state championship. He obviously wants to minimize distractions as they try to finish the job — and, more importantly, he's fully committed to not pulling a Lane Kiffin on his current team.

item.title: Jeffery Simmons excited to play in prime time for Bears, something Titans rarely do
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Jeffery Simmons is ready for prime time.
item.content:encoded:
Jeffery Simmons is ready for prime time.

Simmons, who was traded from the Titans to the Bears this week, will play on Monday night against the Seahawks, and then he'll play next week on Sunday night against the Buccaneers. The Bears are one of the NFL's marquee teams, the league puts them in marquee time slots, and that's a big change for Simmons, who hasn't played a prime time game since 2023.

The Titans have no prime time games on the schedule this year. They had none last year, either. They had one prime time game in 2024, but Simmons missed that one with an elbow injury. The last time Simmons played in prime time was 2023, as the Titans just haven't been a team the NFL wants to promote.

"It's exciting. I haven't played in a prime time game since 2023," Simmons said. "It's been that long since I've played in prime time. I think it was Thursday night against the Steelers, was the last time I actually played in one. It's exciting. When you've got a prime time game it means you're doing something right. With this team, with last year's success and this year, what more can you ask for? To come into this situation, to help this team win big games, meaningful football this time of the year, and also my first game being here in Chicago I get to play on Monday night. I think that's the dream of every NFL player, to come into a situation like this. I'm so excited. I'm excited to be able to go out there Monday night."

Simmons said he's so accustomed to playing at noon Nashville time on Sunday and then getting home in time to watch Sunday Night Football that he sees the prime time games as special, just like the fans do.

"I play at 12 o'clock every Sunday," Simmons said. "To be able to get home and watch the prime time games, then the Thursday night games, you're watching."

A huge national TV audience will be watching Simmons, something that has rarely been the case during his eight-year NFL career.

item.title: After Josh Jacobs was arrested, three other women told police he had abused them, too
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Police records released late on Friday show three women contacted police after Jacobs' May arrest to report similar incidents.
item.content:encoded:
While police were investigating Josh Jacobs following a domestic violence accusation in May, multiple other women reported similar incidents of Jacobs abusing them.

NBC 26 in Green Bay received previously unreleased files in connection with the Jacobs case from the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department late Friday, and those files showed that officers heard from at least three other women who said they had been victims of violence at the hands of Jacobs.

One woman contacted police in June after hearing of Jacobs' May arrest, saying she had been the victim of a similar incident with Jacobs years earlier and was reporting it to police for the first time because she wanted people to believe the woman accusing him in May. That woman said that in January of 2022, Jacobs slapped her across the face, grabbed her by the hair, threw her onto a bed, pinned her down, threw her onto the floor, spit on her and grabbed her by the throat. She also said Jacobs took her phone as she attempted to leave his home.

Another woman also contacted police later in June and said that in April of 2021, Jacobs grabbed her by the arms, pushed her against a wall near a window and threw her belongings outside the home. She said she suffered bruising to her arms and pain and swelling in her rib area. She said she had reported it to the police in a different municipality, and the records released by Hobart-Lawrence Police to NBC 26 indicate that they confirmed with another police department that it did receive that report, but Jacobs apparently was not arrested because the woman had no visible signs of injury.

A third woman told Hobart/Lawrence Police in July that in May of 2022, Jacobs placed his hands on her head and neck, dragged her, scratched her chest, and took her phone. She said she suffered bruising to her arm and scratches to her chest. She said she did not report the incident to police or seek medical attention because Jacobs had told her she could be deported if she had any contact with the authorities.

Jacobs eventually pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property in connection with the May arrest. The NFL placed him on paid leave for the first six games of the season, then allowed him to play starting in Week 7. Jacobs remains subject to a potential NFL suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy, and the accusations brought by the three other women could be considered by the NFL in determining league discipline.

item.title: Report: Philip Rivers has "emerged as the focus" of NC State coaching search
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Six days ago, former NFL (and NC State) quarterback Philip Rivers was identified as a person "expected to be in the mix" for the now-vacant Wolfpack head-coaching job.
item.content:encoded:
Six days ago, former NFL (and NC State) quarterback Philip Rivers was identified as a person "expected to be in the mix" for the now-vacant Wolfpack head-coaching job.

He has now "emerged as the focus" of the search, according to On3.com.

There's reportedly no timetable for the hire, given that Rivers continues to coach high-school football in Alabama.

Rivers's son, Gunner, has committed to attend NC State as a member of the class of 2027.

NC State fired Dave Doeren last Saturday.

Rivers played for the Wolfpack from 2000 to 2003. He was the fourth pick in the 2004 NFL draft, technically selected by the Giants before being sent to the Chargers as part of the Eli Manning trade. Rivers starred for the Chargers from 2004 through 2019. Rivers spent 2020 with the Colts before retiring. He returned last year to start three games for the Colts, after Indianapolis lost starter Daniel Jones to a torn Achilles tendon.

Rivers has been coaching high-school football since 2021. He interviewed for the Bills' head-coaching vacancy earlier this year.

item.title: Jeffery Simmons says calling Caleb Williams "Painted Nails" was "just smack talk"
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: New Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons said his nickname for Caleb Williams two years ago was nothing more than gamesmanship.
item.content:encoded:
New Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons said his nickname for Caleb Williams two years ago was nothing more than gamesmanship.

Simmons, then with the Titans, jokingly referred to Williams as "Painted Nails" in an interview with The Rich Eisen Show. He said Friday that he thought Bears fans were "going to crash my Instagram" after that.

Now, Simmons, Williams and Bears fans are on the same side after the trade from Tennessee.

“I’ve been a fan of Caleb,” Simmons said, via Jason Lieser of the Chicago Sun-Times. “Of course, being on the other side and having to play against him, I’m not going to tell him that. I’m going to talk as much smack as I can.

“But now he’s on my team. Any teammate you ask about me, man, I have my teammate’s back, no matter if he’s on the other side of the ball or not. I’m going to talk the most smack to you when you’ve got a different color jersey on, but when we’re on the same team on Sundays, I go to war for any of my guys in the locker room. I hope Caleb would know that.”

Simmons said he and Williams talked after a joint practice in August and again on Friday morning before meetings. Williams doesn't hold the comment against Simmons.

“The comments a couple years ago about the nails is all part of my game, with the smack talk,” Simmons said. “I don’t know if you guys have heard, but I’m probably one of the best smack talkers. I talk a lot of smack when I’m on the field. I’m looking forward to being his teammate. We all know what type of player he is.”

item.title: Report: Daron Payne has a significant foot injury
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne was expected to have serious trade interest before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne was expected to have serious trade interest before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Alas, Payne, who is in the final year of his contract, is heading to injured reserve instead.

The Commanders added Payne to the injury report Friday, listing him as questionable with a foot injury.

Payne, 29, was diagnosed with a significant injury after injuring his foot in Friday's practice, NFL Media reports. He will undergo an MRI on Sunday to confirm what X-rays showed.

Payne has possibly played his final game this season, per NFL Media.

Washington drafted Payne with the 13th overall pick in 2018, making him the team's longest-tenured player. He started every possible game from 2020-24 and missed only two games last season.

He totaled 14 tackles, five quarterback hits and one sack in six games.

Payne has 38 sacks in his career.

item.title: Jordan Love passes Brett Favre for multi-touchdown games to start season
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Packers have had three starting quarterbacks since Brett Favre replaced Don Majkowski in Week 3 of the 1992 season.
item.content:encoded:
The Packers have had three starting quarterbacks since Brett Favre replaced Don Majkowski in Week 3 of the 1992 season. Favre is in the Hall of Fame, Aaron Rodgers will get in on the first ballot, and Jordan Love is still crafting his legacy.

Love has had some special performances, and some solid runs. His three-touchdown performance on Thursday night gives him the second-longest streak of games with two or more touchdowns to start a season in Packers history, with eight.

Rodgers set the Packers record in 2011, with 15 straight games of two or more touchdowns. Favre had seven straight to start the 1995 season. Both won the NFL MVP in those seasons.

Love is currently at 25-1 to win the 2026 MVP award. On Thursday night, he completed 30 of 41 passes for 288 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception.

For the year, Love currently leads the league in attempts (312), completions (192), yards (2,246), and touchdown passes (16).

item.title: Sean Payton goes for his 200th career win on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Broncos coach Sean Payton, with five wins in 2026, now sits one win short of a milestone only 11 other NFL coaches have achieved.
item.content:encoded:
Broncos coach Sean Payton, with five wins in 2026, now sits one win short of a milestone only 11 other NFL coaches have achieved.

Payton's next win will give him 200 for his career, including the postseason. His first crack at No. 200 comes on Sunday against the Chiefs.

He has coached 319 games, generating a record of 199-120. He's 189-110 in the regular season and 10-10 in the playoffs.

With two more wins, Payton will catch Dan Reeves and Mike Tomlin for 10th on the all-time list. Four more wins after that will put Payton even with Marty Schottenheimer, at 205. Chuck Noll is No. 8 with 209. Paul Brown is No. 7 with 222.

Payton, 62, could eventually catch Tom Landry at No. 5, at 270.

He's also angling to be the first coach to win a Super Bowl with two different teams. Other coaches currently in position to chase that distinction include Giants coach John Harbaugh and Steelers coach Mike McCarthy.

item.title: Falcons sixth-round rookie Anterio Thompson says he was told he'll never play again
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Falcons rookie defensive tackle Anterio Thompson, who has been on the non-football injury list since the start of training camp, has disclosed that his career is over.
item.content:encoded:
Falcons rookie defensive tackle Anterio Thompson, who has been on the non-football injury list since the start of training camp, has disclosed that his career is over.

Via Marc Raimondi of ESPN, Thompson recently disclosed on social media that he has been told he’ll never play football again, due to a genetic mutation of his spinal cord.

Coincidentally, Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski was asked about Thompson on Friday, before Thompson's Instagram post circulated.

"Mentally, I've been better than anyone would be in my situation," Thompson wrote. "As a football player you know one day you'll have to hang up your cleats but you just hope it's on your own terms. It's hard to explain what it feels like to go through the highest of highs to the lowest of lows in the [sic] matter of seconds."

Thompson, who played college football at Washington in 2025, was a sixth-round pick in the 2026 draft.

item.title: Budda Baker says he's focused on the Cowboys, not trade talk
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The trade deadline is Nov. 10, and the Cardinals could be sellers.
item.content:encoded:
The trade deadline is Nov. 10, and the Cardinals could be sellers.

They surely will get calls on safety Budda Baker. The question is: Will they get an offer they can't refuse?

"I just live in the present, like today having a great time with [the media], and going to have a great Friday practice," Baker said, while wearing a Halloween mask, via Darren Urban of the team website. "I'm going to just focus on playing the Dallas Cowboys at their stadium."

Baker, 30, has totaled 44 tackles, an interception, four pass breakups and a career-best 3.5 sacks this season.

He told ESPN this week that he has not asked for a trade, but he hasn't asked not to be traded either. He is under contract through 2027.

item.title: Video seems to contradict Josh Jacobs's explanation of TD celebration
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After Packers running back Josh Jacobs scored his first of two touchdowns on Thursday night, he seemed to celebrate by pretending to be in handcuffs.
item.content:encoded:
After Packers running back Josh Jacobs scored his first of two touchdowns on Thursday night, he seemed to celebrate by pretending to be in handcuffs. That sparked widespread criticism of his apparent effort to trivialize the event that resulted in his May 2026 arrest — an altercation that resulted in a no-contest plea to battery of a female.

Jacobs explained the celebration after the game, claiming it was part of a more elaborate display that the TV cameras didn't fully capture, one that had nothing to do with Jacobs's arrest.

A more lengthy video of the celebration was surfaced, and it doesn't seem to support Jacobs's explanation.

At first, Jacobs has his hands behind his back. Later, Jacobs moves his hands to the front. Teammate Savion Williams seems to unlock the handcuffs that Jacobs says weren't handcuffs.

Even if Jacobs is telling the truth, it's a stunning lack of awareness as to how the celebration would be perceived. And his decision to react to the question by complaining that Prime Video showed "fuckin' one second" of the celebration and that the media is "gonna make it something that it wasn’t" is hardly the kind of contrition he should be displaying, given the broader circumstances.

item.content:encoded:
The Dolphins made a roster change a couple of days before their Week 8 game against the Patriots.

They announced that they have claimed defensive end Jamree Kromah off of waivers. Kromah was cut by the Bears after they traded for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons on Thursday.

Kromah had two tackles and a tackle for loss while playing 28 defensive snaps for the Bears in two appearances this season. That marked his first regular season action since signing with Chicago as an undrafted free agent in 2024.

The Dolphins waived defensive end Rob Beal to make room for Kromah. Beal had 37 tackles and a sack in 27 games for Miami over the last four seasons.

item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Titans ruled out rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
item.content:encoded:
The Titans ruled out rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) for Sunday's game against the Bengals.

Tate missed all three practice days.

"I think it’s a little complicated there, especially for a young guy, [to play without practicing]," coach Robert Saleh said, via Jim Wyatt of the team website.

Tate leads the Titans with 34 catches for 413 yards and a touchdown.

The Titans also ruled out punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) and running back Tyjae Spears (knee).

Veteran Thomas Morstead, signed to the practice squad earlier in the week, will handle the punting this week.

"He's been around, man," Saleh said. "He's funny. I was with him at the Jets, but he's a good man, works his butt off. [Kicker] Joey Slye, I was messing with Joey yesterday, just talking about how I think he's got some competition in the weight room now with the way Thomas works out."

The Titans added cornerback Jaylon Jones (knee) to the injury report with limited work on Friday. He is questionable.

Defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers (groin/back), linebacker Dorian Mausi (foot) and wide receiver Calvin Ridley (hip) are also questionable. Franklin-Myers was limited Friday, while Mausi and Ridley were full participants.

Mausi is in his 21-day return-to-practice window, so the Titans will have to make a roster move for him to play Sunday.

item.title: Kerby Joseph after return to practice: I'm still him; I hope you all ain't forgot
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Lions added cornerback Roger McCreary to their injury report Friday.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions added cornerback Roger McCreary to their injury report Friday. They list him as questionable to play with a foot injury.

Running back Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) both had another full practice Friday and do not have an injury designation. Gibbs and St. Brown missed Wednesday's session.

The only other player besides McCreary with a status is safety Kerby Joseph, who won't play again this week.

The All-Pro player has not played since Week 6 of last season because of a knee injury. He is in his 21-day return-to-practice window.

"Just being back out there felt nostalgic," Joseph said Friday, via Tim Twentyman of the team website. "I haven't practiced in a long time, so this week felt pretty good. I'm still him. I hope you all ain't forget. I'm still him."

Joseph has taken only individual reps thus far but could get "real practice" next week, coach Dan Campbell said.

"That'll be the plan," he said.
